target: implementation execution plan, preamble and tools

decisions.question: How is a phase cut into steps for the ledger?

options.label: Three steps per phase (config, code-plan, implement), two commits each, step ids continuing from S96
options.consequence: One skill invocation per step, as the planning protocol had it; the context and the plan are committed and recorded before any code, so a bad plan is visible on its own. 42 steps for nidana.model.

options.label: One step per phase
options.consequence: Fewer ledger lines, but the context switch, the plan and the code share one artifact commit and one gate, and a context defect is found only after implementation.

decisions.chosen: Three steps per phase (config, code-plan, implement), two commits each, step ids continuing from S96
decisions.why: Each of the three is a separate skill with its own quality gate (hsdd-config's equality check, the derivative's Plan check, the phase gate), and conventions' Execution setup orders them the same way. Continuing the S numbers keeps run.jsonl and the explorer on one sequence.

decisions.question: The decision schema's step enum has only planning steps. How are implementation decisions typed?

options.label: Add config, code-plan and implement to the enum and to ledger.mjs
options.consequence: Implementation decisions are typed by the step that took them, and the judge can calibrate them apart from planning decisions.

options.label: Reuse phase-plan for all of them
options.consequence: No schema change, but plan-time and code-time decisions become indistinguishable in the ledger.

decisions.chosen: Add config, code-plan and implement to the enum and to ledger.mjs
decisions.why: The intake segment added intake the same way (S56). The enum's description says it aligns with the judge's steps, and code decisions are a different population from planning ones.

decisions.question: Which execution method runs each phase's plan: subagent-driven-development or executing-plans?

options.label: subagent-driven-development for every phase
options.consequence: A fresh implementer and a task reviewer per task, and a whole-branch review per phase: the most independent checking the run can buy while nobody watches, at roughly three subagent contexts per task.

options.label: executing-plans in one subagent per phase, then one final review
options.consequence: About a third of the cost; the only independent check before the owner is one final review per phase.

options.label: By tier: SDD for full-review phases, executing-plans for gate-only and spot-check
options.consequence: Saves on the declaration phases (.3 to .5), where the surface and reject replays already check most of the work, but spot-check phases hold real logic (lineage, projection, codec) with no per-task review.

decisions.why: The owner reviews only after the run, so per-task review is the main defence against a wrong turn that later tasks build on. SDD's batching rule still lets same-shape declaration work go to one implementer. The signal that would change it: task reviews in .3 to .5 finding nothing the replays had not, after which the gate-only phases could move to executing-plans.
evidence: superpowers subagent-driven-development SKILL.md, vs. Executing Plans

decisions.question: The planning protocol had the orchestrator run no skill in its own context. Who is SDD's controller?

options.label: The orchestrator
options.consequence: SDD works as designed: the controller dispatches implementers and reviewers. The orchestrator's context carries each phase's plan and the short reports, so it is summarized more often; SDD's progress.md and git make that recoverable.

options.label: One controller subagent per phase
options.consequence: Keeps the orchestrator's context lean, but a subagent cannot dispatch subagents, so the controller would have to implement inline, which is executing-plans under another name.

decisions.why: SDD's controller role exists to dispatch fresh subagents; only the top-level session can. The hsdd-config and writing-plans steps still run in fresh subagents, so the planning protocol's rule holds for every skill that can run in one.
evidence: superpowers subagent-driven-development SKILL.md, The Task Loop
Agent tool: a fork executes directly and does not re-delegate

decisions.question: Which model runs each role? SDD requires the model to be named on every dispatch.

options.label: Opus for plan writing, full-review implementers, fix rounds 4 and 5, final reviews; sonnet for context switches, other implementers, task reviews and re-reviews
options.consequence: The most capable model where design judgement or a whole branch is in play, a strong mid-tier model elsewhere, per SDD's Model Selection.

options.label: Opus everywhere
options.consequence: Simplest and strongest, at several times the cost on mechanical tasks such as transcribing declarations.

options.label: Haiku for transcription tasks
options.consequence: Cheapest, but SDD warns the cheapest models take two to three times the turns on multi-step work; the declaration tasks carry long dartdoc and exact reject codes.

decisions.chosen: Opus for plan writing, full-review implementers, fix rounds 4 and 5, final reviews; sonnet for context switches, other implementers, task reviews and re-reviews
decisions.why: SDD's Model Selection, with mid-tier as the floor for reviewers and prose-driven implementers. Full-review phases (.1, .2, .6, .7, .12) are the replay tool and the analyses, where a subtle bug misleads every later gate.

decisions.question: Where do the phases' commits land?

options.label: Node branch impl/nidana.model from auto/v1-impl-1, a phase branch per phase merged --no-ff, the node branch merged --no-ff into auto/v1-impl-1 at the end
options.consequence: Follows conventions' branch discipline; each phase is one merge commit the owner can review or revert; nothing is pushed.

options.label: Commit everything directly on auto/v1-impl-1
options.consequence: Fewer branch operations, but phases interleave in one line of history and the conventions' per-node integration branch is skipped.

decisions.chosen: Node branch impl/nidana.model from auto/v1-impl-1, a phase branch per phase merged --no-ff, the node branch merged --no-ff into auto/v1-impl-1 at the end
decisions.why: hsdd/conventions.md: one integration branch per node, phase branches merge into it, node branches merge into the root branch, never squashed. The owner created auto/v1-impl-1 as the run's root branch. Local merges of branches the run itself created are not the shared-branch side effect SDD and finishing-a-development-branch ask about.

decisions.question: SDD's setup asks for an isolated workspace through using-git-worktrees. Does each phase get a worktree?

options.label: No worktree; the phase branch in the main checkout
options.consequence: Phases run one at a time, so isolation is the branch; the pub cache, .dart_tool and fvm link stay in one place.

options.label: A worktree per phase
options.consequence: Isolation from the main checkout, at the cost of a fresh pub resolution and analyzer cache per phase and paths that differ from the ones the tools assume.

decisions.chosen: No worktree; the phase branch in the main checkout
decisions.why: Conventions reserve worktrees for phases that run in parallel; this run is serial. SDD's hard rule is never to implement on main, and no phase does.
evidence: hsdd/conventions.md, Companion skills (using-git-worktrees for phases that run in parallel)

decisions.question: Where is each phase's superpowers plan saved?

options.label: docs/superpowers/plans/{phase-id}.md
options.consequence: The path follows from the phase id, so the tools and a resumed orchestrator find it without a search; conventions name plans after their phase.

options.label: docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-{phase-id}.md
options.consequence: writing-plans' dated default; the date changes across a night-long run, so the path has to be looked up.

decisions.why: writing-plans lets the user's location preference override its default, and conventions state the preference: under docs/superpowers/plans/, named after its phase, so two phases never write one plan file.
evidence: hsdd/conventions.md, Execution protocol, Plans are per-phase files and Plan naming
superpowers writing-plans SKILL.md, Save plans to

decisions.question: writing-plans ends by asking the human to review the plan and confirm the execution method. Who takes that hand-off?

options.label: The orchestrator: the derivative's Plan check by script, then SDD's pre-flight scan, with the method fixed in advance
options.consequence: The run keeps going; the plan is checked mechanically for HSDD's constraints and read once by the controller for conflicts between tasks; the owner reviews the committed plan afterwards.

options.label: A separate plan-review subagent before execution
options.consequence: One more independent read per phase, largely duplicating SDD's pre-flight scan and the per-task reviews.

decisions.chosen: The orchestrator: the derivative's Plan check by script, then SDD's pre-flight scan, with the method fixed in advance
decisions.why: The owner is asleep, and the hand-off's two questions are answered: the method by the decision above, the plan's fitness by the Plan check (hsdd-config says to run it before choosing a method) and SDD's scan of every task pair.

decisions.question: finishing-a-development-branch asks which way to integrate a finished branch (merge locally, open a PR, keep, discard). Which, for every phase?

options.label: Merge locally with --no-ff into the node branch, keep the phase branch, push nothing
options.consequence: The next phase builds on the merged result, as its dependencies require; each phase stays one reviewable merge.

options.label: Keep each branch unmerged for the owner
options.consequence: Later phases depend on earlier ones (nidana.model.2 needs .1's tool), so the run could not continue past the first phase.

decisions.chosen: Merge locally with --no-ff into the node branch, keep the phase branch, push nothing
decisions.why: Every phase after the first depends on an earlier one; conventions forbid squash merges of multi-phase work. Pushing is an outside side effect the owner did not ask for.

decisions.question: The verification doc's Sign-off belongs to a human reviewer, and the review gate is not passed while an item lacks a disposition. What does the run do with Sign-off, and does it wait for it before the next phase?

options.label: Leave Sign-off empty for the owner and continue once the gate passes and the final review is closed
options.consequence: Each phase is merged with its evidence but without the human review its tier asks for; the owner signs off afterwards, in the tier's depth, and a phase they reject is reworked on top of the later ones.

options.label: Have the final reviewer subagent fill Sign-off
options.consequence: Every gate condition reads as passed, but a subagent's sign-off would claim a human review that never happened.

decisions.chosen: Leave Sign-off empty for the owner and continue once the gate passes and the final review is closed
decisions.why: hsdd-config's constraint 5 leaves Sign-off for a human reviewer; filling it would misstate who reviewed. The run's own reviews (per task and per branch) are recorded in the SDD flow and in this ledger, and every Outstanding item and Learning still gets the run's proposed disposition for the owner to confirm.

decisions.question: When a phase finds a contract gap (a fixture that fails against an implementation matching the Interface), what does the run do?

options.label: Pause the phase, insert an hsdd-contract step (and hsdd-reconcile when phase ids or a Delivery paragraph move), re-run the switch, resume; decide breaking fixes as the owner's stand-in
options.consequence: Governance changes only through its owning skill, as ADR-001 item 8 and the phase context's Discipline require; each fix is a recorded step the owner can review.

options.label: Let the implementer adjust the fixture inside the phase
options.consequence: Faster, but a phase would edit hsdd/contract/, which ADR-001 item 8 and every phase context forbid, and the fixture would stop being an independent check.

decisions.chosen: Pause the phase, insert an hsdd-contract step (and hsdd-reconcile when phase ids or a Delivery paragraph move), re-run the switch, resume; decide breaking fixes as the owner's stand-in
decisions.why: The Discipline section of every phase context says exactly this, with the human doing the renegotiation; under the owner's no-asking instruction the orchestrator stands in for that human and records it.

decisions.question: Do the run's prose rules (no em-dash, no "load-bearing") apply to code, dartdoc and commit messages, or only to HSDD artifacts?

options.label: To everything committed
options.consequence: One rule everywhere, checked by impl-gate on every added line; dartdoc copied from the contracts already complies.

options.label: Only to HSDD artifacts and plans
options.consequence: Code comments could drift from the owner's prose rules, and the gate would need to tell text from code.

decisions.why: The rules are the owner's prose preferences, not HSDD's; the planning run applied them to every artifact it wrote. A mechanical check on added lines is simple and catches template text such as the verification template's em-dash title.

decisions.question: How does the orchestrator check a phase before merging it?

options.label: A script that checks the write set over the phase's commits, the verification doc, the prose rules and the registries, and runs the phase gate from the context file
options.consequence: The same checks every phase, independent of what any subagent reports; a fresh gate run before every merge, as verification-before-completion requires.

options.label: Trust the last task's gate run and the final review
options.consequence: Cheaper, but the gate output would come from a subagent's report, and a fix wave after the final review would go unverified.

decisions.chosen: A script that checks the write set over the phase's commits, the verification doc, the prose rules and the registries, and runs the phase gate from the context file
decisions.why: The planning run's gate.mjs caught defects the subagents' self-checks missed; HARNESS.md recommends script-made checks. Implementation commits as it goes, so the check runs over a commit range rather than git status.
evidence: docs/auto-run/HARNESS.md, What went wrong, items 6 and 11
